title: Sequence Compression into a Recurrent State

steps.title: Trace how a recurrent model turns a sequence into one evolving summary
steps.topic: Establish that an RNN reads tokens one at a time and carries information forward through a single hidden state.

steps.title: Show why the hidden state becomes a bottleneck as the sequence grows
steps.topic: Explain that every new token must be incorporated into the same fixed channel, causing earlier information to be overwritten or weakened as later tokens arrive.

steps.title: Make long-range information loss concrete without treating it as a failure of tokenization
steps.topic: Use the contrast between an early token and a much later position to show why information needed at the end of a sequence may no longer be recoverable from the recurrent state.

steps.title: Turn the bottleneck into a design requirement for the next architecture
steps.topic: Conclude that a model needs a way for an output position to access relevant input positions directly rather than relying exclusively on one compressed recurrent state, setting up attention without explaining its mechanics yet.

teaches: How recurrent networks process a sequence one token at a time
What the hidden state represents during recurrent processing
Why compressing an entire sequence into one recurrent state creates an information bottleneck
How repeated updates can overwrite or weaken information from earlier tokens
Why direct access to earlier input positions is a useful architectural requirement
plan.opening_promise: After this section, you will be able to trace the information path through a recurrent sequence model, identify where long-range information is compressed or lost, and explain why attention needs to remove that bottleneck.
